h1: SEO cost for a small business: the ₹40,000 starting line
metaTitle: SEO Cost for Small Business: What ₹40,000 Buys
metaDescription: SEO cost for a small business in India starts near ₹40,000 a month. Here's the exact scope that budget funds, and the three things worth cutting first.
answer: SEO for a small business in India starts around ₹40,000 a month — roughly 24 delivered hours, which is one competent generalist for about a day a week. On a 20-page services site in a tier-1 city that funds technical hygiene, local visibility and two researched pages a month. Below ₹25,000 you're buying reports.
takeaways: ₹40,000/mo is about **24 delivered hours** after tools, overhead and margin. Everything on this page is a decision about where those 24 hours go.
Cut the monthly report before you cut the work, cut link outreach before you cut content, and cut content volume before you cut content quality. In that order.
The move from ₹40,000 to ₹75,000 isn't about revenue. It's about whether your constraint has changed from *we have no pages* to *our pages can't outrank anyone*.
Lock-in hurts a small business more than anyone. ₹40,000 on a twelve-month contract is ₹4,80,000 you have already spent, whatever happens in month three.

sections.h2: The site this page is priced around
body: Generic ranges are useless, so here's one concrete shape. It isn't a client — it's the configuration we get asked about most, and everything below is costed against it.

A 20-page services website in a tier-1 city. Five services, one location, WordPress, built in 2021 by someone's cousin and edited nervously ever since. Roughly 40 target queries, most of them carrying a city name. The competition is a dozen local firms plus two national aggregators who outrank everybody on the head term. Two enquiries a week come in through organic search and the founder answers them personally.
That business does not need ₹1,50,000 of SEO a month. It needs about 24 hours of someone competent, applied consistently, for a year. Which is what ₹40,000 buys.

callout.title: How ₹40,000 becomes 24 hours
callout.body: Indian agency delivery cost sits near ₹1,200 per genuinely billable hour once salaries are loaded with PF, gratuity, seat and health cover. Take about 28% off the fee for tools, admin, sales and margin, divide what's left by ₹1,200, and ₹40,000 lands at roughly 24 hours. The same sum on any quote you receive works just as well.

bullets: **That's 22–28 hours, and it's already tight.** Every extra thing you ask for displaces something on this list. There is no slack at ₹40,000 and any agency implying otherwise is planning to underdeliver quietly.
**Nothing here is link building at scale.** Earned links cost hours, and hours are exactly what's scarce. That's a deliberate trade, and for a local services business it's usually the right one.

sections.h2: The three deliverables to cut first when cash is tight
body: When the budget has to come down, most founders cut the retainer and keep the scope, which produces the worst of both. Cut in this order instead — it protects the work that compounds.
numbered: **Cut the monthly report, not the monthly work.** Formal reporting eats two to three hours. Replace it with a live dashboard you can open whenever you like and a 20-minute call. You lose a PDF nobody read past slide four and buy back roughly a page of content a month.

**Cut link outreach before you cut technical or content.** Links compound slowest, which makes them the most painful thing to fund and the most survivable thing to pause. A 20-page local site wins on relevance, Google Business Profile and reviews long before it wins on domain authority. Restart outreach when you're competing outside your city.

**Cut content volume, never content quality.** Two properly researched pages beat four thin ones — and thin pages don't just underperform, they actively drag on how the rest of your site is assessed. If ₹40,000 becomes ₹28,000, ship one good page a month, not three bad ones.

callout.title: The thing people cut first and shouldn't
callout.body: Measurement. Cancelling analytics and rank tracking to save ₹3,000 a month removes your ability to prove any of it worked — which is exactly how sensible retainers get cancelled in month five for no good reason. Keep the baseline even if you pause the work.

sections.h2: When you're genuinely better off doing this yourself
body: We turn down small-business work fairly often, because for a real slice of businesses an agency is the wrong purchase. Four honest tests.
bullets: **One location, under 15 pages, buyers search "near me".** Get your Google Business Profile right, collect reviews properly, write one honest page per service, and you've captured most of what's available. That's a weekend and a monthly habit, not ₹4,80,000 a year.

**You have under ₹25,000 a month to spend.** Don't split it across four disciplines — that funds nothing four times. Hire one freelancer for one defined fix, or do it yourself. [Whether SEO costs money at all](/cost/is-seo-free-or-paid) prices out the DIY version, tools included.
**You sell on referral and the site is a brochure.** If nobody has ever searched for what you do, SEO is not your constraint and no retainer changes that. Fix demand first.

**You can't review content inside two weeks.** An agency will stall in your approval queue and you'll pay full price for the waiting. Founder review time is the real bottleneck in almost every small-business SEO programme.

sections.h2: The point where ₹75,000 starts making more sense
body: The trigger isn't a revenue figure, whatever a sales deck told you. It's a change in what's actually blocking you. At ₹40,000 the constraint is usually *we don't have enough good pages*. At ₹75,000 it's *our pages exist but can't outrank anyone*, and that second problem needs different people, not more hours from the same one.

The arithmetic is worth doing anyway. ₹40,000/mo is ₹4,80,000 a year ex-GST. If a new customer is worth ₹25,000 in gross profit to you, that's about 20 customers a year — under two a month — to break even. ₹75,000/mo is ₹9,00,000 a year, so 36 customers, three a month. Plug in your own gross profit figure; the point is that the second number has to be genuinely reachable before you commit to it.

Four signals that the step up is the right call: you're chasing queries without a city modifier, your site has passed roughly 60 pages, two competitors are publishing weekly, or you've opened a second location.

sections.h2: Why a small business should refuse lock-in outright
body: Long contracts get sold with a true argument: SEO takes time and an agency that can be fired in month two won't invest properly. Fine. They also exist because they insulate agency revenue from agency underperformance, and a small business carries that risk far worse than a funded company does. ₹40,000 a month on a twelve-month contract is ₹4,80,000 you have already spent, whatever happens in month three.

The honest version is a short commitment plus a reason to stay. Ours: SEO from **₹75,000/mo**, smaller sites from **₹40,000/mo**, ex-GST. Month-to-month after the first quarter, 30 days' notice, and you keep every asset — content, links, dashboards, documentation, accounts — regardless of how it ends.

And the commitment that replaces a lock-in: on day one we freeze your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search. If we haven't beaten that number in 90 days, we keep working free until we do. We never promise a specific ranking position for a specific keyword — nobody controls Google's index. It's also why we take only three new clients a month, because that risk doesn't survive volume.

If a freelancer is the better fit at your budget, we'll say so. [Agency versus freelancer](/compare/agency-vs-freelancer) makes the case both ways, [what local SEO costs](/cost/local-seo-cost) goes deeper on single-city businesses, and [our pricing](/pricing) has the full card.

faqs.q: How much should a small business spend on SEO per month in India?
faqs.a: ₹40,000 a month is a realistic starting line for a 20-to-40-page site in a competitive city — about 24 delivered hours. Under ₹25,000, spend it on one specific fix with one freelancer rather than splitting it across four disciplines, where it funds nothing four times over.

faqs.q: Is ₹15,000 a month enough for small business SEO?
faqs.a: It's about nine delivered hours once tools, overhead and margin come out. That covers reporting, some title tags and a status call. It won't fix site architecture, produce researched content or earn links. It isn't fraud, it's arithmetic — the problem is that the proposal rarely says so.

faqs.q: How long before a small business sees results from SEO?
faqs.a: Impressions on target queries should move within four to eight weeks. Real ranking movement on local queries takes three to four months, national ones three to six. Google Business Profile work is the fastest-moving part and can shift map pack visibility inside a month if the profile was neglected.

faqs.q: Can a small business do SEO without an agency?
faqs.a: For one location, under 15 pages, and buyers who search "near me" — genuinely yes. A correct Google Business Profile, real reviews, fast mobile pages and one honest page per service covers most of what's available. Agencies earn their fee when the work becomes continuous and needs four specialisms at once.

faqs.q: What should be in a small business SEO package?
faqs.a: Technical hygiene and Search Console monitoring, Google Business Profile and citations, two researched pages a month, on-page and internal linking, some local outreach, and a dashboard plus a working call. If a package at this price promises all that plus aggressive link building, something is being skipped.

faqs.q: Should a small business sign a 12-month SEO contract?
faqs.a: No. Commit for a quarter — long enough for the work to be fair to judge — then keep it month-to-month with 30 days' notice. A twelve-month contract at ₹40,000 is a ₹4,80,000 decision made on the strength of one sales call, and it protects the agency's revenue rather than your outcome.
